sources.title: Camera-Based Coaxial Melt Pool Monitoring Data Registration for Laser Powder Bed Fusion Additive Manufacturing
sources.authors: Yan Lu, Zhuo Yang, Ho Yeung, Jaehyuk Kim, Hyunbo Cho
sources.relevantFinding: The open AMMT registration path embeds camera triggers in the xy2-100 command stream, calibrates fixed delays, and aligns each image frame to a laser-spot position. The preprocessing flow explicitly requires scanning for missing or corrupted frames before registration.
sources.boundaryForRc44: The method presumes that the corresponding frame is available after missing-frame preprocessing. It does not establish how to infer which trigger is absent when a released AVI exposes no per-frame trigger key.

sources.title: Spatiotemporal Monitoring of Melt-Pool Variations in Metal-Based Additive Manufacturing
sources.authors: Siqi Zhang, Yan Lu, Paul Witherell, Soundar Kumara, Hui Yang
sources.relevantFinding: Scan-direction knowledge is used to rotate and align melt-pool tails before tensor decomposition and additive-Gaussian-process monitoring. This confirms that direction-conditioned image dynamics can carry process-path structure.
sources.boundaryForRc44: The paper analyzes a stream already aligned to the scanning path; it does not test dropped-frame identity or distinguish deletion from clock slip.

sources.title: Statistical and Spatio-temporal Data Features in Melt Pool Monitoring of Additive Manufacturing
sources.authors: Brandon Lane, Ho Yeung, Zhuo Yang
sources.relevantFinding: Registered image frames can be reduced to physics-motivated spatial and temporal features and superimposed on part coordinates.
sources.boundaryForRc44: Feature extraction and fusion rely on established temporal correspondence; they do not validate correspondence after frame loss.

sources.title: Drop-DTW: Aligning Common Signal Between Sequences While Dropping Outliers
sources.authors: Mikita Dvornik, Isma Hadji, Konstantinos G. Derpanis, Animesh Garg, Allan D. Jepson
sources.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 34
sources.relevantFinding: A single dynamic program can align shared sequence signal while dropping interspersed outliers, providing a concrete alternative to standard DTW when observations are absent or extraneous.
sources.boundaryForRc44: Its experiments concern instructional video and audiovisual retrieval, not AMMT command-camera registration. Transfer to X16 requires a domain-specific observable and independent positive controls.

sources.title: Overhang Part X16 In-Situ Process Monitoring Data
sources.relevantFinding: The public record supplies byte sizes, hashes, and URLs for separate XYPT, AVI, and TIFF archives spanning 250 layers.
sources.boundaryForRc44: The record authenticates archive-level objects but does not publish a trigger-to-frame identity ledger.

confirmedFacts: NIST's registration workflow treats missing or corrupted frame detection as preprocessing rather than deriving missing identities from the AVI header.
Scan direction and temporal image features are physically motivated observables for registered melt-pool streams.
Outlier-dropping dynamic programming exists as a general sequence-alignment method.
synthesis.inference: Combining command-derived dynamics, low-resolution image dynamics, known synthetic deletions, and set-valued dynamic-programming adjudication is a testable bridge for X16's missing-identity gap.
synthesis.unverifiedProposal: The combined bridge may narrow L0001's 23 missing positions. No reviewed source located in this audit reports that exact X16 experiment, and no novelty claim is made.
synthesis.searchBoundary: This compact audit is sufficient to prevent presenting the ingredients as new. It is not a systematic review of all citation descendants, patents, theses, or proprietary AM monitoring systems.
